title: Auto repair for Together GPU Clusters: from GPU fault to healthy node
gist: Together AI explains its automatic GPU node repair for GPU clusters: continuous passive health checks inside the VM and on the host, evidence-gated policy-driven repairs on an escalation ladder, layered safety rails against alert storms, and automatic re-validation of vacated hardware.

insights.claim: Together AI's auto repair follows the rule that no node repair occurs without a failed health check behind it, because the NotReady signal cannot distinguish a broken node from a briefly unreachable one nor indicate whether to reboot or replace.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Evidence-based remediation differentiates GPU cloud reliability from basic auto-replace.
insights.quote: no node repair occurs without a failed health check behind it, and every repair carries its supporting evidence

insights.claim: Because GPUs are passed through to customer VMs, detection runs on both sides of the hypervisor: in-VM exporters watch kernel logs for Xid errors, DCGM for ECC and thermal issues, and Node Problem Detector, while the host monitors InfiniBand rails and reachability.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: GPU fault classes (Xid, ECC, PCIe, IB flaps) drive cluster downtime economics.

insights.claim: The system separates observed from actionable alerts: every repair-relevant alert marks a node Degraded, but only signals with an action mapping create a repair, and unmapped alerts are logged and sent to support.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Prevents pointless reboots such as for disk pressure.

insights.claim: Customers decide whether and when repairs happen: the default is Approve before repair, with optional fully automatic mode, per-fault and per-Xid-code consent, and Wait for idle with a default maximum wait of 2 hours capped at 24.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Operator control over disruption is key to adoption in training clusters.

insights.claim: Repairs escalate on a ladder of reboot, quick reprovision, migrate to new host and human-only remove; after the same action runs twice for a fault on one machine, the next recommendation moves one rung up.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Bounded retries reduce repeated downtime on flaky hardware.
insights.quote: Two tries per rung, then one rung up.

insights.claim: Migration consumes real capacity so it requires a critical alert firing now or within ten days on the same machine; otherwise it runs as a quick reprovision, and clusters can reserve hot spare capacity for guaranteed replacement windows.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Spare-capacity reservation is a priced SLA lever for GPU clouds.

insights.claim: Teams can bring their own detectors such as NVSentinel via API, console or node labels (preview); detector name plus request ID is the idempotency key, so a re-asserting detector cannot reboot a node twice.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Open integration lowers switching cost for fleets with in-house tooling.

insights.claim: Layered rails assume alert storms: signal persistence, roughly 30-minute cooldown, a concurrency budget, one repair per node pool at a time, a circuit breaker for correlated bursts and one target per repair.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Cluster-level causes such as bad driver pushes must not trigger mass node churn.
insights.quote: Many nodes failing at once points to a cluster-level cause, and repairing nodes one by one will not fix it.

insights.claim: Hosts vacated by migration or removal are automatically re-validated with the same GPU, NCCL, InfiniBand and storage checks as new machines, and only an explicit failure files a hardware ticket.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Automated re-validation cuts RMA noise and keeps healthy capacity in the pool.
insights.quote: Only an explicit failure files a hardware ticket.

insights.claim: Some faults such as Xid 79 need the GPU to lose power, which a VM reboot cannot do, so Together is previewing host power cycles instead of consuming a new host.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Reduces capacity burn on recoverable hardware.

insights.claim: Repair decisions key on alerts, nodes and machines rather than GPU vendor, so adding a new accelerator needs only new detection exporters and a diagnostic battery.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Signals readiness for multi-vendor accelerator fleets.
insights.locator: Built to extend past one accelerator

insights.claim: Next on the roadmap: NVSwitch SXid coverage, repair status written back to node metadata, and a unified health surface linking failed checks to repairs.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
insights.so_what: Indicates reliability tooling investment for NVLink-class fabrics.

source_meta.author: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Dongsheng Zhang, Barbara Kazanowska
